explanation: The theorem says the permutation representation k[G/H] is projective in Rep k G when H is finite and |H| is invertible in k. The closest Mathlib result is the instance in Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/FinGroupCharZero.lean (Rep.instProjective). It says every Rep k H is projective when H is finite and NeZero (Nat.card H : k). That only gives projectivity of the trivial H-representation. It does not give projectivity of the induced permutation module on G/H. The library's own lemma projective_permutation, which is the real content, needs an additional argument. I found no Mathlib lemma that gives projectivity of Rep.ofMulAction k G (G ⧸ H), or that induced or coinduced representations preserve projectivity. I searched Rep/*.lean for ofMulAction and permutation, and searched Mathlib for Projective together with ofMulAction, ind and Ind. The only related hit was diagonal_succ_projective in Rep/Iso.lean. That is the case of G acting on Fin n → G, so it does not cover this statement.
